analysis.title: Emerging Markets Morning Pulse, 12 November 2026
key_insights: EM credit was subdued on 11 November: the US Veterans' Day holiday and no cash Treasury trading cut liquidity and client activity across regions.
LATAM was largely inactive, with only limited private banking demand for short-dated oil names on very low volume. Brazilian sovereigns and corporates saw virtually no trading.
BEEFBZ remained under pressure ahead of its 3Q26 earnings release after the close. BRASKEM stayed in focus after reports that creditors presented two restructuring proposals.

MENA primary: Boubyan Bank announced an AT1 mandate (PerpNC5.5 Sukuk, IPT 7.875%, desk fair value about 7.50%). Al Rayan Bank mandated an inaugural $500m 5-year Sukuk at T+150 area, which the desk expects to tighten to about +125bps.
Turkish credit traded quietly with limited client flows, concentrated in corporates while financials stayed subdued.

CEE credit showed resilience despite pressure on EUR rates. The new NOVALJ euro perpetual drew two-way interest and closed 0.20 to 0.40pts above reoffer. The desk says the focus today is rates, and how Bunds open will set the tone after the sharp selloff before the US holiday.

Rates: US Treasuries edged higher in the morning on safe-haven demand tied to concerns about Nvidia's leadership, partly offsetting expectations of tighter Fed policy. The 10-year yield fell 1bp to 4.98% and the 30-year fell as much as 3bps to 5.32%.
Treasury futures weakened on Wednesday after hotter-than-expected US inflation data and hawkish Fed commentary. Markets fully price a 25bp Fed hike in December, with a small probability of 50bp.

Equities: global equities gave back part of Wednesday's gains on the leadership crisis at Nvidia. S&P 500 futures fell 0.4% and Nasdaq 100 futures fell 0.9%, after the indices rose 1.3% and 2.3% on Wednesday. Nvidia fell as much as 10% after hours on uncertainty around CEO Jensen Huang, overshadowing CoreWeave's 25% surge.

FX: the Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index rose 0.4% on Wednesday to its highest in 18 months on the inflation data and hawkish Fed expectations. EUR/USD 1.1080 (-0.7% on Wednesday), GBP/USD 1.3274 (-0.5%), USD/JPY 159.70 near the 160 level after the yen fell 0.7%. Indonesia's rupiah hit a record low amid dollar strength and concern over a potential MSCI exclusion of Indonesian equities.
Oil fell in the morning on rising Middle Eastern production and subdued US-Iran hostilities. WTI -1.5% to $85.24, Brent near $91.

market_movers.rationale: Shares fell as much as 10% after hours on uncertainty around CEO Jensen Huang, which weighed on tech and AI sentiment.
CoreWeave surged 25% on Wednesday on renewed AI optimism and industry developments.

earnings_insights: BEEFBZ (Brazilian beef producer) reports 3Q26 results after the close on 12 Nov. Its bonds were under pressure beforehand.
NATURA reports numbers after the market on 12 Nov. The desk says the result could trigger trading in the name and show how the Brazilian consumer is doing.
